title: The Value of Last-Mile Delivery in Online Retail
eligible_reason: The underlying design is a textbook staggered DiD (customer-month panel, home delivery rolled out to pickup stations month by month from April 2021, about 33% of customers treated across 12 monthly cohorts, 67% never treated, customer and month FE, two-way clustering), but every main-text TWFE column (Tables 2-4) includes the additional treatment regressor is_first_treat (D_it x First, a first-treated-month spike dummy) and Tables 3-4 add subgroup-by-treatment interactions (customer type, city tier) and month x type FE. The protocol excludes extra treatment regressors and subgroup-by-treatment interactions. The Callaway-Sant'Anna event study (csdid.R) and the plain-TWFE spillover regression (Table B4) are online-appendix items (Figures B1, Table B4), so no main-text specification qualifies. In addition, the package ships only synthetic data, so nothing can be replicated.
design_notes: synthetic_panel.csv: 10,000 customers x 24 months (Apr 2020 - Mar 2022, month_index 0-23); real data were 100,000 customers (generator comment). treated = customer-level assignment; first_treat_month in 12..23 (12 monthly cohorts, peak August 2021 = month 16); D_it = treated x (month >= first_treat_month); is_first_treat = 1 in the first treated month only; D_sta = station has any treated customer by month t. Table 2 (lines 105-117): reghdfe y d_it is_first_treat, absorb(customer_id month) vce(cluster customer_id month) for orders, log_orders, log_spending, log_order_value. Table 3 (135-147): c.d_it#i.type c.is_first_treat#i.type with month#type FE. Table 4 (166-190): d_it + d_it x tier1 + d_it x tier3 + is_first_treat x type within customer-type subsamples. Appendix: B2/B3 city-time and station-time FE (still with is_first_treat); B4 spillover on never-treated customers (d_sta only, customer + month FE, no controls: eligible-looking but appendix); B5 uniform-timing D_unif (single date); B6 aweight by pre-period orders; B7 alternative transformations; B8 winsorized outcomes; B1 1:1 matched sample with match_weight. csdid.R: att_gt(yname=log_orders/log_spending, gname=cohort (0 for never treated), idname=customer_id, tname=month_index, xformla=~1, est_method='reg', control_group='notyettreated'), aggte dynamic -6..6 (Figure B1). sdid.R: synthetic DiD placebo (Figure B2). causalml/ and vrp/ are not DiD.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Synthetic generator: ADOPTION_PROBS over month_index 12-23 (Apr 2021 - Mar 2022); README says the synthetic data preserve the real staggered adoption timing.
modern_estimators_named: callaway_santanna (did::att_gt, not-yet-treated controls, Figure B1, appendix)

data_files_note: README: 'All data necessary to reproduce the results are included in the replication package in synthetic form, generated by the authors.' Original Cainiao/Alibaba data proprietary and not shared.
software_notes: Stata (reghdfe, outreg2) for tables; R (did, synthdid, ggplot2) for Figures B1-B2; Python (pandas, causal ML, routing) for the rest.
priority_note: No main-text spec without the D x First regressor or interactions; appendix CSA/spillover specs would qualify but only synthetic data are available.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text; manuscript.pdf is in the package but was not read for this screen). If the published main text reports the CSA event study (Figure B1) or a column without is_first_treat, eligibility should be revisited; replication would still be blocked by the synthetic data.
